task: Phase 6 Step 5 -- Hirist block-classifier forensics, offline only, zero network requests

1_exact_classifier_function.operates_on: complete raw HTML document source (page.content()), not visible/rendered text
1_exact_classifier_function.code: lowered = html.lower(); for phrase in _HARD_BLOCK_PHRASES: if phrase in lowered: return ("BLOCKED", phrase); for phrase in _CHALLENGE_PHRASES: if phrase in lowered: return ("SOFT_BLOCK_OR_CHALLENGE", phrase); return (None, None)

3_exact_occurrence_context.reason: the Step 4 validation driver captured and persisted only derived data (html_length, classifier state, matched_block_phrase, parsed job list) -- the actual fetched HTML body was never written to any file; the temporary driver and its output were deleted at the end of Step 4 per standard scratchpad cleanup practice
3_exact_occurrence_context.what_is_determinable_instead: the matching mechanism itself scans the entire raw document, so by construction an attribute/script/comment/JSON-LD match is just as possible as a visible-text match -- see section 6

5_evidence_from_step1_successful_page.check_performed: captchaOrChallenge marker against page.locator('body').innerText() (visible/rendered text only)
5_evidence_from_step1_successful_page.caveat: Step 1 and Step 4 are two separate live requests at different times; page content (especially third-party ad/tracking scripts) can legitimately differ between requests even at near-identical total length -- this is strong circumstantial evidence, not proof that Step 4's raw HTML also lacked the word in visible text

6_comparison_of_two_pages.conclusion: the differing outcome is consistent with either a genuine content difference between requests, or the same underlying content being present both times but only detectable by the raw-HTML check -- available evidence alone cannot fully distinguish these, but section 7 provides strong independent reason to favor the latter

verified_precedent_in_this_project.source: scripts/naukri_parser.py, pre-existing docstrings (written for unrelated reasons, months before this investigation)
verified_precedent_in_this_project.quote_1: Classify a captured page as blocked or not, based only on human-visible text (title + body) -- never on raw HTML source, tag attributes, CSS, or script content.
verified_precedent_in_this_project.quote_2: Guessing at keyword rules for conditions never actually observed is exactly how an earlier naive, raw-HTML keyword check produced false positives on this same search-results fixture.
verified_precedent_in_this_project.quote_3: On search_results_sre_bengaluru.html, that naive approach 'sees' the words 'captcha' and 'verify' inside a dormant .bot-guard-captcha CSS rule and an otpMobileVerifyContainer class name -- neither of which a human visitor ever sees rendered on the page.

independently_reverified_this_task.method: plain-text grep against a local, already-present fixture file, zero network access

second_independent_precedent.finding: data-recaptcha-v3-integration-lix-value="control" present in LinkedIn's own page meta config, on a page confirmed reachable with no actual block or challenge shown

7_does_captcha_occur_in_normal_page_cont.pattern_identified: major job-board/commercial sites commonly ship reCAPTCHA-family bot-protection tooling (CSS classes, JS libraries, config flags) site-wide, present in raw markup whether or not actively shown to a given visitor -- confirmed across two independent sources (Naukri, LinkedIn) in this same project's own captured data

decisive_executable_proof_added_this_tas.method: synthetic, in-memory HTML only, zero network
decisive_executable_proof_added_this_tas.finding: a page with a fully valid, parseable schema.org ItemList (one real job entry) plus a <style> block containing a .bot-guard-captcha-style CSS class name IS, right now, with the current unmodified hirist_parser.py, incorrectly classified as SOFT_BLOCK_OR_CHALLENGE instead of VALID_RESULTS
decisive_executable_proof_added_this_tas.positive_control: a second fixture with the word genuinely in visible body text correctly classifies as SOFT_BLOCK_OR_CHALLENGE, confirming the defect is about WHERE the word appears, not that the word itself is unreliable
decisive_executable_proof_added_this_tas.note: does not and cannot prove this specific mechanism is what happened in the actual Step 4 response (section 3's evidence gap remains: the real HTML was never saved), but eliminates doubt that the classifier's design is capable of exactly this false positive on a genuinely valid Hirist-shaped page
